### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**15** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via account_name (literal, a string literal in FieldSchema))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const), ObjectSchemaBase (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via renamedFrom (symbol, a field of const object FIELD_KEY_STORAGE_CLASS; a field of const object FIELD_REFERENCE_POSITIONS), account_name (literal, a string literal in FieldSchema), renamedFrom (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in refuseDishonestRenamedFrom))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `da1e1cc2bd079a3852ac8ef6f1025ac74a958e6b` — the merge of head `4ad4222ab8dafc79f152c5c0f2294ee9798a3505` into base `26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin da1e1cc2bd079a3852ac8ef6f1025ac74a958e6b && git checkout da1e1cc2bd079a3852ac8ef6f1025ac74a958e6b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383 4ad4222ab8dafc79f152c5c0f2294ee9798a3505 && git checkout -B drift-repro 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383 && git merge --no-ff 4ad4222ab8dafc79f152c5c0f2294ee9798a3505

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4ad4222ab8dafc79f152c5c0f2294ee9798a3505`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/field.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, content/docs/references/data/field.mdx, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx, content/docs/references/system/migration.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, .changeset/30880-field-renamed-from.md; read to judge them: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (the extension merge, `mergeObjectDefinitions`, and `validate`), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts (`BUILTIN_COLUMNS`), packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts (`BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts (the `field` item door), packages/spec/liveness/README.md (the `planned` / `authorWarn` rules)

Rendered 2026-11-06T12:45Z on the net diff of the head against its merge base with `main` (`d55acb78`; `main` has not moved on any touched path since), the card and its comments, the cloud#3652 rulings Q3 「默认拒绝，需显式映射（推荐）」 and D3 「写进清单 renamedFrom」, record 6259332195 item 5, the bodies of #30884 and #30885, and the head's check-runs read once. The dev's report and the seat's conclusions were not used as evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The accept-set widening is exactly the declared one — right.** `FieldSchema` (a `strictObject`) gains one optional `z.array(z.string().regex(...))` with no default; no other key moves. `ObjectSchema`'s new refinement only refuses inside the new key's domain. The driver-sql and metadata-core hunks are classification rows in two maps pinned exhaustive over `FieldSchema.shape`; neither changes an accept/refuse door. The `/meta/types` field property count 82 → 83 matches one new key.
- **The five rules — right and complete against the card's list.** Grammar: `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`, the `FieldSchema.name` / `FieldNameKeySchema` regex, judged in `FieldSchema` at `renamedFrom.INDEX`. Own key: `entry === fieldName`, the map key (right, since `FieldSchema.name` is optional). Repeat: a per-list `seen` set, reported on the later index. Live key: `hasOwnProperty(fieldMap, entry)`. Claimed twice: a per-object `claimedBy` map, reported on the later claimant naming the first. The map half skips entries that fail the grammar, so a non-key entry gets one issue, not two. Each check returns after its issue, so one entry yields one issue. Order is sound: `seen.add` precedes the live-key check, so `['status','status']` beside a live `status` reports a live-key issue at 0 and a repeat at 1.
- **An object without the key parses byte-identically — right.** `.optional()` with no `.default()`, nothing materializes; the pin asserts `hasOwnProperty === false` on every parsed field.
- **The refusals name the object, the field and the old key — right for the four map-half rules** (`Field \`x\` on object \`y\` declares \`renamedFrom\` entry 'z', REASON PRESCRIPTION`). The grammar refusal names the entry only; the PR discloses it and the issue path locates the field, and `FieldSchema` cannot see the object. An object with no `name` is rendered as the word unnamed. Accepted deviation from the card's letter on rule 1; no fix owed.
- **`ObjectExtensionSchema.fields` runs only the field half — right as described, and the gap is real but not exploitable on this head.** Measured: `ObjectExtensionSchema` parses `z.record(FieldNameKeySchema, FieldSchema)` and its own `superRefine` does not call `refuseDishonestRenamedFrom`; the objectql registry's `validate('object')` runs `ObjectSchema.parse` on the owner's declaration, and `mergeObjectDefinitions` folds extension fields into the merged definition without re-parsing the merged object through `ObjectSchema`. So an extension field carrying `renamedFrom: ['a']` where the owner still declares `a`, or where the owner's new version just dropped `a`, parses clean. Nothing reads the key on this head, so no data moves; but the second shape is a cross-package column capture once #30885 reads the merged map (see ④). `fieldPatches` cannot carry the key: `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST.field` is `label, description, inlineHelpText, placeholder`.
- **The strict-schema publish-time consequence — stated honestly, and acceptable.** The PR body, the changeset and the card all say an artifact carrying the key is refused as `unrecognized_keys` by every runtime older than this release. It is opt-in per package, and a package that does not write it is unaffected. The refusal on an older runtime is zod's generic unknown-key sentence, which this side cannot improve. The `.describe()` itself does not say it; the changeset does, which is where an author reads release consequences. Acceptable.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` **minor** — right: `Metadata-protocol: added` (a new authorable key) takes at least minor on the package the diff moves.
- `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/metadata-core` **patch** — right: each gains one classification row in an exhaustive map and no protocol change; AGENTS.md's rule reads `none` takes patch.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` — right; the claim's `none` was wrong and the body corrects it. One kind only, so no `narrowed`/`semantic` precedence question.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right; no accepted manifest is refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(a) The interim gap — acceptable; not a should-fix.** The liveness README makes a `planned` row warn only with `authorWarn: true`, and every precedent `planned` field row (`conditionalFormatting`, `options[].kind`, `referenceDeletedWhen`, formerly `percentDisplay`) carries none. The card rules none. The `.describe()`, the docs row and the changeset each carry the inert-until-the-execution-ships sentence, so the author reads it where they write the key. One wording note, no fix owed: the ledger note states #30884's refusal as the reason the key is never silently inert, but that refusal does not exist until #30884 lands; between this landing and #30884 the key is inert and only the prose says so. The row's `note` is for ledger maintainers, so no author is misled.
- **(b) `storage` in `FIELD_KEY_STORAGE_CLASS` — right, by the table's own rule.** The header classifies by what the DDL would read, and keeps intent-class keys the DDL does not read yet (`precision`, `scale`, `deleteBehavior`) as `storage`. The side effect is one true sentence: an author who writes `renamedFrom` on a field keyed `id`, `created_at` or `updated_at` is told the storage half is discarded, which is so, since the platform's own column takes no data from an old one. Acceptable.
- **(c) Skills teaching deferred — acceptable.** The `Skills-docs:` line is on the body and the changeset. A skill that taught the key before any upgrade performs the rename would teach a no-op. The teaching belongs with the first card that makes the key observable to an author, #30884's plan or #30885's execution; #30885 is named and is the ledger's flip. No fix owed here.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against rulings Q3 and D3, the key's first consumers as #30884 and #30885 specify them, and the cited code at the head.

- **Chain a → b → c across versions — holds.** v3 lists `['a', 'b']` (the describe and docs say a field renamed twice lists both), so an installer at v1 or v2 reaches v3 by one carry. An author who lists only `['b']` leaves a v1 installer with a dropped `a` and an added `c` and no link, which #30884 reports as a suspected rename and refuses by default under Q3: a refusal, not silent loss. Order inside the list carries no meaning, and none is needed, since the carry keys off the physical column present. The parse cannot judge a dishonest cross-version history (`c: ['b']` beside `d: ['a']`), and rightly does not: it needs the installed version, which is #30884's plan.
- **A rename to a key an extension adds — a gap for the reader, should-fix (carried to #30885).** Two shapes, both parse clean on this head (see ①): (i) the owner's v2 declares `b: renamedFrom ['a']` while an extension still adds `a`; in the merged map `a` is live, so #30885's precondition (the object no longer declares `a`) fails and the declaration is silently a no-op rather than refused. (ii) An extension field `b__c: renamedFrom ['a']` claims the owner's just-dropped `a`; #30885's stated rule (the table has `a`, none for `b__c`, the object no longer declares `a`) would carry the vendor's column into another package's field. The protocol cannot close this at parse: the extension door does not see the target map, and the merge does not re-parse. **Should-fix:** #30885's acceptance should carry two refusals before any write, an entry naming a key that is live in the merged map (names the extension), and an entry whose old column belongs to another package's history (the carry stays inside the declaring package); and this PR's describe or the ledger note should say the map half is judged on the owner's declaration only, so the reader must judge the merged map. Not a must-fix: nothing reads the key on this head, and the card scopes the checks to the object.
- **Platform-owned column names as entries — should-fix (carried to #30885, or a sixth parse rule).** `renamedFrom: ['id']`, `['created_at']`, `['updated_at']`, or the tenant column, parses clean: those names are never in the author's `fields` map, so the live-key rule cannot see them, and `BUILTIN_COLUMNS` lives in driver-sql (`schema-drift.ts`), which the spec cannot import. Under #30885's stated rule (the table has the column, the object does not declare it), such an entry would carry the primary key or an audit column into an author's field. The card's five rules are honoured exactly; this is a hole in the rule list, not the implementation. **Should-fix:** #30885 refuses an entry naming a platform-owned column before any write; alternatively a spec-side reserved-name set judged in `refuseDishonestRenamedFrom` on a follow-up to this card. Not a must-fix for the same reason: inert on this head.
- **Case-sensitivity — holds.** The grammar is lowercase-only, so `Company` is refused at `renamedFrom.0`; every field key the map can hold is lowercase, so no earlier key could have been mixed-case. The map half compares exact strings, which is right once both sides are in the grammar.
- **Rename plus type change — does not blur Q3 on this head; one question for #30884.** The parse judges no type, the describe says the upgrade plan judges the old column's type, and #30884 lists a declared rename whose types the drift categories call `destructive` as a type-change finding too. The question for #30884: a declared rename whose type change is `needs_confirm` rather than `destructive` reads, under its Expected 1 as written, as a planned rename with no confirmation, which Q3 would otherwise refuse. `renamedFrom` must not be read as a type-change confirmation. Escalated to #30884; nothing owed on this PR.
- **Removal of `renamedFrom` in a later version — degrades to a refusal, not to loss; should-fix on the docs, one sentence.** v3 drops the key from `b`: an installer at v2 sees no change; an installer at v1 sees `a` dropped and `b` added with no link, a suspected rename refused by default. Safe. The docs row and describe do not tell the author to keep the entry for as long as any installed version may still carry the old key; one sentence in `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` would. Low.

### Check-runs on the head, read once

38 completed success (among them Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, PR-body guards, Test Core 3/5/6/8). 8 skipped by their own conditions. 16 in_progress at the read, NOT MEASURED: Test Core 1, 2, 4 and 7 of 8, Test UI 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 of 16, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace.

### Findings, one line each

1. should-fix (carried to #30885): the extension door runs the field half only and the merge does not re-parse, so the reader must refuse an entry live in the merged map and keep the carry inside the declaring package.
2. should-fix (carried to #30885, or a sixth parse rule on a follow-up): an entry naming a platform-owned column (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, the tenant column) parses clean.
3. should-fix (docs, one sentence): tell the author to keep a `renamedFrom` entry while any installed version may still carry the old key.
4. escalated to #30884: a declared rename must not stand in for a type-change confirmation when the type change is `needs_confirm`.
No must-fix.
